This compact member of the family Columbidae is found across the southern United States, including Florida, where it commonly inhabits open fields, scrub, coastal dunes, woodland edges, neighborhoods, and other areas with exposed ground and nearby cover.

Common Ground Doves are primarily ground foragers that feed on seeds and grains. Their sandy-brown plumage, dark wing spots, short tail, and subtle scaling on the breast help distinguish them from larger doves. When flushed, the wings can reveal rich reddish-brown coloration.

This interactive model is useful for studying avian anatomy, bird identification, morphology, camouflage, feeding adaptations, and Florida biodiversity.

description:
An interactive 3D model of a domestic chicken (Gallus gallus domesticus), presented as an educational specimen for studying avian anatomy, morphology, and external features.

The model allows viewers to examine the chicken from all angles, including the head, beak, comb, wattles, wings, plumage, legs, feet, and overall body proportions. Chickens are members of the family Phasianidae and are domesticated descendants of wild junglefowl.

name: Great Blue Heron
description:
A 3D model of a Great Blue Heron (*Ardea herodias*), one of the largest and most recognizable wading birds in North America. Great Blue Herons are common throughout Florida and are frequently found along marshes, estuaries, mangrove shorelines, ponds, canals, and other shallow-water habitats.

Their long legs allow them to wade slowly through shallow water, while the long, pointed bill is adapted for capturing fish, amphibians, crustaceans, and other aquatic prey. Great Blue Herons often remain motionless while hunting before striking rapidly with the bill.

This interactive model allows viewers to examine the heron's elongated neck, spear-like bill, long legs and toes, body proportions, plumage, and characteristic wading-bird anatomy. It is useful for studying bird identification, structure and function, wetland ecology, and adaptations to aquatic environments.

name: Brown Pelican on Channel Marker
description:
A 3D model of a Brown Pelican (*Pelecanus occidentalis*) perched on a marine channel marker post above the water. Brown Pelicans are large coastal seabirds commonly seen throughout Florida, where they inhabit beaches, bays, estuaries, mangrove shorelines, and other coastal environments.

Unlike most pelicans, Brown Pelicans typically capture fish by plunge-diving from the air, using their long bill and expandable throat pouch to scoop prey from the water. Their webbed feet are adapted for swimming, while docks, pilings, channel markers, and other structures provide convenient resting and observation sites.

This model allows viewers to examine the pelican's distinctive bill and throat pouch, webbed feet, body proportions, plumage, and characteristic posture while perched on a structure typical of Florida's coastal waterways.

name: Willet — Coastal Shorebird
description:
The Willet (*Tringa semipalmata*) is a relatively large member of the sandpiper family and a familiar shorebird along Florida's coast.

Willets are generally gray above and white below, although breeding birds develop more extensive brown-gray mottling and speckling. Their long, straight bill is well suited for probing wet sand, shallow water, and mud for prey. The legs are typically blue-gray.

One of the Willet's most recognizable characteristics becomes visible when the bird takes flight. Its wings display a bold black-and-white pattern, with a conspicuous white stripe contrasting strongly against darker portions of the wing. This pattern can make a flying Willet much easier to identify than a resting bird.
